title: Tie runs are sorted by deeper keys before the merge sort
body:
`sort_partition` in `libsufr/src/build.rs` sorts each partition by its 64-bit key and hands every run of equal keys to `KeyScheme::order_ties`. For `UnmaskedKeys` that calls `merge_sort`, which compares suffixes from the first character. Suffixes in a run share the key's characters, 21 for DNA, so every comparison in the run re-reads them. `MaskedKeys::order_ties` orders its runs without `merge_sort`.

## Proposal

A `sort_run` that encodes a second key at `start + depth` for each suffix of a run, sorts the run by it, reads the LCP between unequal keys as `depth + shared`, and recurses into the ties with the depth grown by the key's characters, handing a run to `merge_sort` only past a fixed depth. `merge_sort` and `merge` take a floor, the characters the run is known to share, and `find_lcp` starts past it. The proposal first handed a run to `merge_sort` under a mask or past the cap as well. A mask is now ordered by `MaskedKeys::order_ties`, and b3f9104 removed the cap.

## Rejected

Measured on 2026-11-05 with the floor at 128 characters, 10 MiB fixtures, 4 threads, median of 5, against 8a05eb2, the parent of b3f9104, so with the build-time cap still in place: normal 1.03x, protein 1.08x, long-n 1.41x with peak memory 85 to 218 MiB, long-repeats 1.49x. Each level allocates a key per suffix of the run and the recursion holds every level's keys alive, which is the memory on long-n, whose runs of N are one giant tie run. On long-repeats every suffix sits in a run of ten copies, and six levels of keys per run cost more than the merge sort, whose LCP cache answers those comparisons at once. The patch is `tmp-claude/2026-11-05-construct-refactor/floor-and-deeper.patch`.

## Open

Whether a size threshold, deeper keys only for runs over some length, keeps a win on unmasked tie runs without the loss on repeats. Not tried. This issue first named the capped case as the place the idea won. b3f9104 removed that case on 2026-11-05, after the measurements.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/fdde2c6d
notes.text: Kept open by Jack on 2026-11-05. A query length cap is a first-class feature and the benchmark suite has no row with one, so the suite's four rows do not measure the case this and the floor in sufr-1422ef are for. On dna-100.fa with --dna -m 20 the floor alone took the build from 1.21 to 1.15 s. The working tree is back at 8a05eb2; both patches are under tmp-claude/2026-11-05-construct-refactor/.
